examples.text: Um übrigens die Brauchbarkeit der beyden Lehrbücher, so viel an mir liegt, zu befördern, und der Theilnahme, welche sie gefunden, mehr und mehr zu rechtfertigen, werde ich gleich, wenn der Druck dieser kleinern Grammatik wird zu Ende seyn, anfangen die Hülfsbücher für beyde auszuarbeiten; […]
examples.ref: 1819, Friedrich Thiersch, “Vorrede zur zweyten Auflage”, in Griechische Grammatik zum Gebrauch für Anfänger, 2nd edition, Leipzig: Gerhard Fleischer der Jüngere:
examples.english: To furthermore increase the usefulness of the two instructional books, as much as I am able, and to increasingly justify the audience they have found, I will, as soon as the printing of this smaller grammar has finished, start to work on the companion books for both; […]
examples.translation: To furthermore increase the usefulness of the two instructional books, as much as I am able, and to increasingly justify the audience they have found, I will, as soon as the printing of this smaller grammar has finished, start to work on the companion books for both; […]

examples.text: Von hier aus können Sie mit einem kleinem Handelsschiff und einem Scout die außerhalb des Atolls liegenden Inseln erforschen.
examples.ref: 2007, Katja Tischer, Das große inoffizielle Handbuch zu Anno 1701, Anno 1503, 1602 und allen Addons, Markt+Technik Verlag, page 150:
examples.english: From here you can explore the islands outside of the atoll with a small trading ship and a scout.
examples.translation: From here you can explore the islands outside of the atoll with a small trading ship and a scout.

examples.text: Einige Schritte weiter überquert der Prospekt die Eisenbahnlinie nach Adler und das Tal eines kleines Flusses.
examples.ref: 2014, Andreas Sternfeldt, Sotschi: Russische Schwarzmeerküste und Kaukasus, Trescher Verlag Berlin, page 94:
examples.english: A few steps further on, the prospekt crosses the railway line to Adler and the valley of a small river.
examples.translation: A few steps further on, the prospekt crosses the railway line to Adler and the valley of a small river.

raw.etymology_text:
Inherited from Middle High German klein, kleine, from Old High German kleini, from Proto-West Germanic *klainī (“shining, fine, splendid, tender”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *gleh₁y- (“to cleave, stick”).
Cognate with Dutch klein and English clean. Doublet of clean. For a similar semantic development, cf. zierlich (orig. "decorative", today "petite").
